generated_text: Honestly, Rach, I’m still recovering from Saturday. That night out with the girls was… a lot. I think I need a week just to de-age. A lot good, or a lot… exhausting? You looked a bit peaky when you dropped off the cake this morning. Definitely the latter. Sarah had brought that ridiculously strong tequila. And then Chloe started karaoke. You know Chloe – she thinks she’s Adele. The whole pub ended up singing along, badly. My ears are still ringing. Oh, classic Chloe. She's a whirlwind, isn't she? Little Leo clearly benefited from the quiet though – he’s been surprisingly well-behaved today. He is, isn’t he? A little angel. Though he did try to eat the remote control earlier. I’m just glad he hasn’t discovered his hands yet – that's a whole new level of chaos. Tell me about it! Remember when Finn was that age? He used to try and shove anything and everything in his mouth. Socks, crayons, my lipstick… the list goes on. Oh god, yes. He was a proper explorer. Speaking of the kids, have you heard anything from Jamie? He was supposed to be calling about that rugby trial. No, not a peep. Typical. Probably glued to that computer playing games. I did see a picture of Sophie on Instagram, though. She looks gorgeous. That new haircut really suits her. It does. She's growing up so fast. Time flies. We should really take them away somewhere, shouldn’t we? Just a family break. Definitely. Somewhere sunny, ideally. Maybe Cornwall? We could rent a little cottage. Cornwall sounds lovely. Though, organising it all… that’s the killer, isn’t it? Especially with my work being so unpredictable. I know. It’s a nightmare trying to juggle everything. How’s the proofreading coming along? Are you still swamped? Drowning! That new client is a nightmare. They keep sending me documents riddled with typos and formatting errors. It's like I'm doing their job for them. I was thinking about raising my rates actually. Good for you! Don't let them take advantage. You’re brilliant at what you do. Maybe it’s time you truly valued yourself. You always know what to say. Speaking of birthdays… Mum’s turning 70 next month! We need to start planning something proper, not just a small family dinner. Oh, wow!

Right, so you’re saying flying between countries is  still  cheaper than the train? Even with Brexit making everything a faff? Absolutely. I was looking at getting from Birmingham to Amsterdam for my conference next month, and a return flight's about eighty quid. The train, with all the changes…it's nudging three hundred. Mad, isn't it? Honestly! I was thinking of popping over to Brussels for a weekend. Just a quick jaunt. But the prices… it’s almost tempting to just stick to the Yorkshire Dales. See? And it’s not like we’re talking about luxury flights, either. Budget airlines, all the bells and whistles extra. It’s just… cheaper to fly. Remember when we used to just  drive  everywhere? Like, proper road trips through France and Germany? Feels like a distant memory. Aye, good times. We did that Berlin one, didn’t we? Remember that dodgy motel we ended up in? The one with the pet parrot that wouldn't shut up? Oh god, yes! Carl, that bird nearly drove us insane. Squawking away at 3 AM. I swear it was mocking us. He was probably just lonely. Anyway, driving was the way to do it. Stop where you wanted, see what you wanted. Now, it feels like… even the border controls are extra complicated. They are. I went to Prague last year, and even though the Czech Republic is in the Schengen area, it felt… different. More questions at passport control, more scrutiny. Not aggressively, but noticeably. Exactly! It used to be you could just wander across borders and barely realize you’d changed countries. Now, it’s proper paperwork. I was in Denmark a few years back – brilliant cycling, by the way, you should go – and even then, it felt a little… harder. Like you had to justify being there. I've noticed that. I think it’s a psychological thing as much as anything. It's just not as seamless as it used to be. It used to be so easy to just pop over and see friends living in other countries. Now there's an extra layer of… something. Pre-Brexit, I remember just hopping on the Eurostar to Paris for lunch. Spontaneous, you know? Pop over, have some snails, be back in time for tea. Snails. You and your snails. No thanks. But yes, you’re right. That casualness is gone.

Right, so, decisions, decisions. Eton mess or sticky toffee pudding tonight? Eton mess! Eton mess! Strawberries! Sticky toffee. See? A house divided. Luckily, I've got both ingredients. But we need a consensus. Sticky toffee's a bit heavier, don't you think? It’s a bit rainy outside too. Eton mess is fluffy! And you can put sprinkles on it! Sticky toffee has… sauce. Loads of sauce. True, true. Okay, let's think. We played Monopoly for hours yesterday, and all I remember is you two arguing over Park Lane. Maybe something light and refreshing will counteract all that financial stress. I was  going  to buy Park Lane! You kept landing on it! You landed on it eight times, darling! And you weren’t paying attention to saving your money. Remember when you bought Mayfair with practically nothing left? You laughed! I did, a little bit! But you were very determined. Now, about dessert… Eton mess sounds most sensible. But, to appease the sticky toffee fan… What? How about we have Eton mess, and I’ll make a teeny tiny little pot of sticky toffee sauce on the side? Just for you, my sweet. Really? Just for me? Absolutely. It’ll be our little secret. And then maybe we can finally finish that Monopoly game later, but  no  arguments about Park Lane, okay? We’ll set a rule. A rule? What rule? No arguing about properties for at least five turns. And if you break the rule, you lose a thousand pounds. How’s that? That’s fair! But… what if I land on Park Lane… and I really want it? Then you strategically save your money. Think ahead, darling! You're a budding capitalist, remember? Like Daddy. Though, maybe not  quite  as strategic as Daddy... I am a very strategic capitalist! You are silly. Very silly. Now, Eton mess it is! And a teeny pot of sticky toffee sauce. Ready to help with the strawberries, my two little financiers? Ready! Me too! Can I lick the bowl? Maybe later, little one. First, we need to make it. And then… we'll conquer the world of Monopoly! Hopefully without too many financial meltdowns. We'll be rich! I'm going to buy Boardwalk! Wonderful dreams, my loves. Wonderful dreams. Okay, wash your hands! Deserts await! Yay! Yay! My life is never dull. Speaking of money, what are we doing for school trip funding, Charlie?

Honestly, this traffic is brutal. I swear, it’s worse than a Saturday market in Newcastle. Dramatic as ever, love. It’s just a bit of congestion. We’ll be at Mum's in no time. Did you remember to grab the trifle ingredients? Aye, I did. Got the sherry, the jelly, the spotty custard... the works. Aunt Brenda will be thrilled. Though, I’m still not entirely convinced about her obsession with those plastic cherries. They look like miniature eyeballs. She likes them. It’s a Brenda thing. Besides, the trifle wouldn't be a Brenda trifle without them. So, anything interesting happen at work today? Still wrestling with that linguistic anomaly in the Wordsworth collection? You have  no  idea. Right, so, like, I'm trying to build a model of early 19th-century dialect expressions related to weather, right? And I keep finding these bizarre phrases that don't fit. Like, “a peely-wail sky.” A  peely-wail  sky! What does that even mean? I’ve checked every dictionary, every historical linguistic database… nothing. Peely-wail... Sounds unpleasant. Like something you'd encounter on a particularly grey day in, oh, I don’t know, Yorkshire? Exactly! My best guess is it’s a regionalism, a really obscure one. But I can’t pinpoint the region, or the meaning! It throws the whole model off. And my supervisor's breathing down my neck because the deadline’s next week. That sounds awful, honestly. You’re putting way too much pressure on yourself. A “peely-wail” sky… Maybe it’s not about the weather at all? Maybe it's metaphorical? Like, a sickly, weeping sky? You might be onto something! I hadn’t considered the metaphorical aspect. Though, honestly, after hours of staring at scanned manuscripts, my brain feels like a soggy biscuit. I just want to sit down and eat a massive plate of chips. You and me both. You know, I had a bit of a weird day myself. Old Mr. Abernathy, the client from Birmingham, insisted on calling me "young man" the entire time. Even though his beard is longer than mine. Oh, the classic patronizing 'young man' routine! What did you do? I just smiled and nodded, mostly. Tried to steer the conversation back to bridge specifications. It’s exhausting dealing with people who think they know everything, isn’t it? At least with linguistics, you’re dealing with evidence.

Morning, you two. Not a lot in the papers today. More of the same, really. Morning, Arthur. Never is. Just a rehash of yesterday’s worries, dressed up in new headlines. Morning, dears. I've made a pot of Earl Grey. Arthur, you want yours strong as usual? Please, Margaret. Strong enough to stand a spoon up in. You're a marvel, really. These aches in my knees are playing up something awful today. Damp’s got into 'em, Arthur. Always says that. Damp’s the bane of Norfolk, you know. Eats into the bones. Don’t listen to him, Arthur. He says that to everyone. It's just the weather changing, dear. Here's your tea. Well, he's not wrong about the damp. This house… it’s always felt a bit… clammy. Even when the sun's shining. Reminds me of that project I worked on up near the coast, back in ‘86. New housing estate, practically built on marshland. Marshland, eh? They call it 'sustainable development' now. Then they just built right over it and waited for the problems to start. Oh, leave it be, George. Arthur’s just remembering something from his working days. It's nice to hear about those, isn't it, Arthur? It was a mess, that. Constant subsidence. We spent more time fixing foundations than we did building houses. The council kept complaining about the budget, of course. Typical. Councils. Always complaining. Never had a spare penny for anything sensible, did they? You two and councils. It's a well-worn topic. Speaking of sensible things, I was thinking of making a Victoria sponge tomorrow. Got some lovely fresh raspberries from the market yesterday. Oh, now that’s a good idea, Margaret. Haven’t had a proper Victoria sponge in ages. Not like the ones Mum used to make, of course. She had a knack... Your mother's sponge was something special, Evelyn. That’s true. Light as a feather. Unlike that dreadful one they sell at the supermarket. They pack it with margarine and artificial flavourings. Exactly! It's an insult to baking, it is. I’ll use proper butter, as always. And a touch of vanilla extract. Makes all the difference. Vanilla extract... yes, that’s the key. Those supermarkets, they just don’t know how to do things properly anymore. Remember old Mrs. Peterson? Down the road? Used to make a lemon drizzle cake that could cure anything.

So, tell me everything. Seriously. How’s Honest Skincare doing  really  doing? Last time we spoke, you were still wrestling with the website. Honestly? It's a rollercoaster. The website’s… better. Still not perfect, you know? The product descriptions are finally sounding less like a student essay and more engaging, but the checkout process is still dodgy sometimes. I’ve had two complaints this week alone about it freezing up. Oh no! That’s awful. Have you got someone looking at it? Can’t you just… tweak it? I’m trying, but I'm not exactly a tech wizard, am I? I’m paying a freelancer, but he keeps saying it needs a complete overhaul. Ridiculous expense when I'm barely breaking even most months. The ingredients are costing a fortune too, especially the shea butter. Supply chain issues, apparently. Tell me about it! Everything’s more expensive. But you’ve been getting good reviews, haven’t you? I saw a lovely one on Instagram about the face mask. Yeah, the reviews are mostly positive, which is encouraging. But positive reviews don’t pay the bills, do they? I’ve been trying TikTok, but it’s so much harder than Instagram. People want these super fast, flashy videos, and I'm just… awkward. I tried doing a demonstration of the cleansing oil, and I looked like a complete fool. Don’t be silly! You're you, and people like that. Authenticity goes a long way. Have you considered doing tutorials? Showing people how to incorporate the products into their routine? I thought about it. It's just... time. I’m juggling production, packaging, shipping, Instagram, TikTok… sometimes I feel like I’m going to collapse. Mum’s been a huge help with the packaging, bless her. Your mum’s a star. And you’re doing brilliantly, seriously. Starting a business is  hard . What about Etsy? Have you looked at listing there? I considered it, but the fees… and it feels a bit… impersonal, you know? I want people to feel like they’re buying from a real person, a small business with a story. I completely get that. Have you thought about partnering with any local businesses? Like, maybe offering your products in a boutique or a salon? That’s a good idea! I was chatting to Sarah at “Bloom” recently. She runs a little florist shop in the Jewellery Quarter.

That’s lovely tea, Arthur. Just what I needed. Everything’s been a bit… much lately. Glad you think so, Margaret. I tried a new blend. What’s been “much”? You haven’t been out and about, have you? You know I worry about you when you’re venturing too far. Oh, not venturing far, dear. It’s just… the news, you know? It’s constant doom and gloom. Ukraine, the cost of living… it’s enough to give anyone a headache. Honestly, I spend half my day switching it off completely. I know, it’s dreadful. I try to keep up, but sometimes it’s just too overwhelming. Did you see that piece about the energy prices again? Absolutely ridiculous. I did. Makes you want to go back to the days when a cup of tea didn't cost the earth. Remember when we were kids, Arthur? A penny for a sweet! Oh, yes! And we'd save our pennies for a bag of sherbet lemons. Simpler times, weren’t they? So, how are you managing with things? The heating’s not been on too much, has it? I'm managing, dear. I’m careful. I've layered up, got the blankets out. It’s a bit nippy, of course, but I cope. It’s the worry that gets to you, you know? Wondering how everything’s going to balance. Don't you worry about that. I’ll make sure you’re alright. I can pop over with some extra blankets later, if you like. And perhaps a few tins of soup? Oh, Arthur, you're a dear. You always were. But I really am alright. It’s just… I keep thinking about young Thomas. He's been struggling, hasn't he? With that small business. He has, hasn't he? Terribly difficult out there for small businesses right now. I spoke to him just last week. Trying to be encouraging, you know? Tell him to keep his chin up. He's a good lad, Thomas. Pity his wife isn't a bit... more supportive. Always seems to be a bit down on him. Well, women can be like that sometimes, Margaret. Trying to keep their families grounded, perhaps. Don’t let it worry you too much. Perhaps. It’s just… I want him to be happy. And secure. He deserves a bit of good fortune. He will, Margaret. He's a hard worker.

Speaker_1 : "Honestly, I've never known December to be so mild. It feels… wrong, somehow. I’m practically sweating in here!" Speaker_2 : "Tell me about it! I had to turn the heating right down this afternoon. Can’t believe we’re complaining about being too warm in December. Remember last year’s Christmas? We were shivering!" Speaker_3 : "It  is  a bit odd, innit? Down in Swindon, it's been drizzly but comparatively mild too. Though, my mum keeps saying it's a sign of the apocalypse." Speaker_4 : "Aye, apocalypse or not, good for the mulberries! Had a proper bumper crop this year. My nan's been making jam like a woman possessed." “Mulberries, you say? Reminds me, I need to add that to my grocery list. We’re having your roast chicken tonight Daniel, are you happy?” “Perfect, thanks El. It was a brave move, opting for chicken. Everyone expects turkey at Christmas, you know.” “It’s lovely! I'm still stuffed from the starters, though. That cheese was incredible, Eleanor." “Glad you like it. I found a really interesting cheddar at Borough Market last week. Thinking about it…speaking of interesting finds, have you two been following that article about the archaeological dig near Bath? Incredible stuff.” "Archaeology? Nah, bit outside my realm, love. I’m more into the practical stuff. Been finally getting around to organising my workshop, actually. Found a right gem of a vintage chisel – proper sharp, too." “A chisel, eh? What kind of making are you into these days, Rhys? Still doing the furniture stuff?” “Yeah, mostly. But branching out a bit. Trying my hand at some decorative metalwork now. Got a commission for a bespoke garden gate." “That's brilliant! You’re so talented. I wish I had a creative bone in my body. All I do is read and write about historical linguistics.” “Don’t sell yourself short, Chloe. That's pretty impressive in its own right. I'm always wishing I had grasped languages better at school!" “Speaking of wishing… Heard old Mr. Henderson down the street is finally thinking about retirement. Shocking, really. He’s been the postman since forever.” "Oh, really? That’s sad in a way. It’s those familiar faces that make a community, isn’t it?” "Aye, that’s right. Lots of changes going on. Makes you appreciate the constants. Like a good teaspoon and a decent cup of tea.”

“Honestly, Mum, I’ve been trying to find matching cutlery for weeks. It’s a nightmare. Half the forks are bent, and the teaspoons are all different shapes.”      “Aye, well, your dad’s been using them to dig in the garden again, hasn’t he, Arthur? He thinks they’re trowels now!"  She sighs dramatically, shaking her head  “Men and their ways, eh?"      “Now, Brenda, that’s not fair! I needed something to loosen the soil, and the cutlery was handy. Besides, they’re just old bits and pieces.”  He gestures dismissively with his fork.       "I think it’s charming, Elara! A bit quirky, you know? Not everything needs to be perfectly coordinated. It's got character."  He grins at Elara.       "Character, is it? In me day, we had one set. One good set. Lasted a lifetime. Didn't fiddle about with fancy shapes and clever designs. Just a good, solid fork."      “Grandad George, that’s lovely, but I’m trying to set up the flat properly. It’s not home until you've got a decent set of cutlery, you know? I was thinking maybe stainless steel, simple design…”      “Stainless steel’s lovely, duck. But it’s expensive. You could always check the charity shops. I got a lovely set of china cups there last month, for a fiver!”      “Charity shops are full of junk, Brenda. You’re wasting your time. I tell you what, I’ll have a look down at the market on Saturday.”      “The market? Dad, you'll be haggling over spoons like you're buying a vintage car. Elara needs something presentable, not a mismatched collection.”      “Liam’s right, Dad. Although, a vintage collection  would  be a bit cool…”  She trails off, considering.  "Remember what Hannah said the other day, about that antique store in town?"      "Hannah? Whose Hannah? That friend of yours from university? The one who’s always going on about ethical sourcing?"  She raises an eyebrow skeptically.       “Yeah, Hannah. She mentioned they sometimes have vintage silverware. It would be a project, but it could be interesting."      “Silverware? Hmph. Heavy stuff. Backache waiting to happen. And you’ll be polishing it 'till the cows come home. Give me plastic any day. Lightweight, easy to clean.”      “Plastic cutlery? George, you’re losing your marbles! What will people think? You’ll be serving dinner with plastic forks and spoons, like a picnic in the park.”      “Arthur, leave the poor man alone.

Mmm, this is lovely, isn’t it, darling? Simple but really tasty. It's good, Mummy. Can I have more cheese? Of course, love. There you go. So, I had a proper chat with Mr. Davies today. About… well, about you knowing more about the new software than he does. Did you tell him I'm good at computers? I did. I explained that you’ve been teaching me a few things actually, about that photo editing program. He seemed a bit… taken aback, to be honest. A bit ruffled. Ruffled like a duck? Exactly like a duck! But in a good way. He said he appreciates the… outside perspective. And that they might actually need you to help train some of the newer staff. Really? Would I get to go to the office? We'll see, sweetheart. It's just a thought at the moment. But it would be lovely, wouldn’t it? You’d be a little tech guru! I like that! Guru! Right, moving onto more exciting things… Have you been checking the weather for Austria? Is it snowy there? It  should  be! That's the whole point, isn't it? I was looking at the forecasts earlier, and it’s looking pretty good for the week we’re going. Lots of sunshine and snow. Will there be snowmen? Can I build a snowman? A really, really big one? Absolutely. We'll build the biggest snowman Austria has ever seen! I've already booked the ski lessons for you, you know. Will Daddy teach me? He promised he would, didn't he? Although, I think he might need a few lessons himself first! Daddy’s not a good skier! That’s putting it mildly. But he’s a very enthusiastic one! And that's what matters, isn't it? Can we get hot chocolate with marshmallows on the mountain? Of course, darling. Mountains of hot chocolate with mountains of marshmallows. And maybe some apple strudel too? Yes! Apple strudel and snowmen! And teaching Mr. Davies about computers! It sounds like a wonderful holiday. Just the ticket. Now, finish your pasta, and then we can look at which ski outfit you want to choose. You’ve got so many! Just one more thing, did you remember to pack your ski gloves? The ones with the glitter on? I forgot! We'll make sure it goes in before we go to the airport.

Ugh, I’m so ready for the weekend. This week has been brutal. Tell me about it! Maths was a nightmare today. Mr. Davies just kept throwing equations at us. Like, seriously? I know! And the fractions… I feel like I’m back in Year 7. I swear, I understood fractions before, but now… brain blank. Me too! I spent half the lesson staring out the window, pretending Ms. Peterson’s cat was doing algebra. You’re awful! But I get it. At least English wasn't too bad today. We finally finished  Macbeth . Yeah, that was pretty good. I actually liked it a lot more than I thought I would. Lady Macbeth is seriously intense. Right? You wonder what would have happened if she hadn’t... you know. Exactly! Anyway, what are you planning for Saturday? Anything exciting happening? Nothing much, I think. Probably just chill, listen to music. I’m finally getting into that new Olivia Rodrigo album. Have you heard it? Yeah! It’s so good. I’ve been listening to it non-stop. I’m obsessed with “vampire.” Same! It’s practically my new anthem. Speaking of music, I was thinking about auditioning for the school band next year. Seriously? That’s awesome! What instrument would you play? I'm thinking flute. My grandma had one, and I used to mess around with it when I was little. I’m not very good yet though, that’s the problem. You could join the beginners' group! It’s pretty relaxed. My cousin’s in it, and he says it's brilliant fun. What about you? Any thoughts on what you want to do after school? Honestly, no clue. It’s all so overwhelming. Like, careers fairs and university applications... I know, right? I've been thinking about maybe doing something in fashion. But I'm worried about getting a job. Yeah, everyone says careers in fashion are really competitive. What about Spanish? You were talking about studying abroad, weren’t you? Yeah, still thinking about it. I actually did quite well on the last Spanish test. Mrs. Garcia said I have a good ear for languages. That's amazing! You should definitely go for it. Imagine, living in Barcelona! I know! But then I think about the money… and the whole leaving-home thing. It’s scary. It definitely is. Remember last year in Food Tech? That disastrous attempt at making soufflés?

Honestly, darling, that new Ridley Scott film…  Napoleon . It’s far too long. Far too long. Really? I heard good things. Joaquin Phoenix is brilliant, isn’t he? Joaquin Phoenix, yes, he’s marvelous, as always. Him and Vanessa Kirby. But two and a half hours! You're practically comatose by the end. They could have trimmed it down, you know? Got to the point quicker. Two and a half hours? Wow. I was expecting something lengthy, given the subject matter. Well, it was a bit… meandering. Flashbacks, battles that felt repetitive. It needed tightening up. You know like when they used to dress actors in those silly wigs in old films? Oh, absolutely! That's what I love about older films, the ridiculousness sometimes. Have you seen "Cleopatra" with Elizabeth Taylor? Oh,  Cleopatra ! A classic. Monumental, absolutely monumental. But expensive! That film practically bankrupted 20th Century Fox. Still, Elizabeth was luminous. Though I always thought Richard Burton was a bit… bland, really. I disagree! I think he had a brooding intensity. But truthfully, it’s Taylor’s film. It's always going to be. Did you ever see "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?"? That's got such intensity. "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?" Yes, of course. Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton again. Brilliant, absolutely brilliant. Terribly depressing, of course, but brilliant. Albee was a genius, wasn't he? Raw. I used to watch that with my friend Doris back in the day. We’d have a bottle of sherry and talk for hours about it. Sherry? Fancy! I’m more of a gin and tonic girl myself. But seriously, you should try to put "Napoleon" aside. It’s not a bad film, just…indulgent. What about "Oppenheimer"? Did you see that? "Oppenheimer"! Ah, yes. Now  that  was something. Nolan’s at the top of his game, isn’t he? Utterly gripping. I felt quite drained afterwards, you know? Dealing with that kind of subject matter… the weight of it all. Definitely. It's long too, but it feels different – more urgent, somehow. Plus, Cillian Murphy is incredible. That look in his eyes... Oh, he  is  fantastic. Gives you chills. It reminded me a bit of Laurence Olivier, in his own way. Such brooding intensity. Have you seen Olivier in "Hamlet" though,  the  Hamlet? Of course! Every student has to! It's iconic. I actually prefer Branagh’s version though.

Right, so, let's nail down this weekend then. Dad's confirmed he’s free for Sunday lunch, yeah? Aye, said he was looking forward to it. He's been moaning about the weather all week, poor love. Says his back's playing up with all this damp. Tell him to take it easy. It's ridiculous, this rain. Honestly, I used to love a bit of drizzle, but this is non-stop. Makes driving a nightmare. I nearly clipped a car yesterday coming home - proper blind spot in this weather. You be careful, love. You know I worry about you driving those long distances. Is that new car treating you alright though? Seems a bit…fancy for you. It is, isn’t it? I needed something reliable. And the heated seats are a godsend in this weather! Definitely worth the extra bit of…well, you know. Worth the extra bit of what, dear? Don't tell me you're back to scrimping again. You deserve a treat. With that teaching salary... Not scrimping, exactly. Just...being sensible. It’s a bit tight at the moment. Student loans, you know. They never really go away, do they? And I'm still trying to pay off that overdraft. Honestly, the way these banks are. I’ve been dealing with their letters all my working life. Sneaky charges, the lot of ‘em. Remember when they tried to charge me for looking at my balance? The cheek! At least court proceedings are fairly straightforward. Black and white, mostly. That’s good, isn’t it? Some certainty. It must be interesting though, seeing all sorts of cases. It is, in a way. Sad mostly. Plenty of people struggling, you know. Young people especially. Like you with your student loans. Footing the bill for their education, then facing a future burdened with debt. It’s not right. It's not. But hey, at least I’m teaching them something useful. Speaking of which, I've got a new class starting on Monday. A group of Year Eights. Nervous wreck already. Year Eights! Oh, bless. That’s a tricky age. All hormones and bluster. Just try to be patient, love. They'll come around. Remember when you were that age? Argumentative as anything! Don’t remind me! Dad used to say I had a mouth on me. Still think he’s right sometimes. Anyway, back to the weekend.

Honestly, the light here is just incredible, isn’t it? Like something out of a painting. It is. Especially at this time of day. Though I’m craving a decent cup of tea afterward. This city has…challenges when it comes to a good cuppa. Tell me about it. I nearly wept when I found that little place near the university selling Yorkshire Tea. It felt like a lifeline. Did you manage to get the silk scarves you wanted? Almost. There was a stall overflowing with them, absolutely gorgeous colours. But the vendor was quoting prices that felt…ambitious, even for silk. I haggled, of course, but I think I walked away paying a bit more than I should have. You always do, darling. You're a terrible negotiator. Remember that jade bracelet in Hong Kong? Hey! That was a perfectly reasonable price. And it's beautiful. Besides, you got a better deal on that antique teacup you were after. Fair point. But seriously, you need to work on your bargaining skills. It's practically a survival skill here. Speaking of survival, how’s the grading going? Still drowning in student essays? Drowning is an understatement. It’s like a tidal wave of grammar and confused arguments. I think I may need to schedule a full weekend just to mark those history papers. Are you managing better with your literature module? Slightly. Though trying to convince them that symbolism isn't just about finding random objects and declaring them 'significant' is proving difficult. One student actually wrote an essay arguing that the colour blue in ‘Hamlet’ represented the character's angst. Oh, bless. That's… certainly a perspective. I'm half tempted to assign a paper on semiotics just to beat some sense into them. Don’t encourage them! They'd just write a paper analysing the semiotics of their lunch. Right, almost home. Do you want me to pick up some more of those steamed buns from that bakery we like? They're on special tonight. Yes, please! I’m absolutely starving. And maybe some mangoes? I’m craving something sweet. Mangoes it is. I’ll also try and look for some decent Earl Grey while I’m there. It’s proving harder to find than you’d think. You’re a saint. Better than our old thing, that was like sitting on bricks. Agnes: Don’t you start complaining, Arthur. You were moaning about the comfort of your armchair just last week. You’ll be saying it's too soft to sleep in next! Eleanor: Mum, leave him be! He's enjoying himself. Now, Thomas, about that plumber. He needs to come round next week to look at that dripping tap in the downstairs loo. Are you free to be in on Tuesday afternoon? Thomas: Tuesday afternoon's my history lesson. After school. Eleanor: Right. Wednesday then? Would that work better? Thomas: Yeah, Wednesday’s fine. Can I get a takeaway that day? Eleanor: You can negotiate with your aunt, yes. As long as you clear up your room first. It's a right tip, lad. Arthur: Tip. Young people today. No sense of tidiness. Back in my day... Agnes: Arthur, don’t start with the "back in my day" stories again. We’ve heard them all a thousand times. Just be grateful Eleanor keeps a clean house. Eleanor: Mum, honestly! Anyway, I’ve been thinking, we need to get some new towels. The ones we have are looking a bit threadbare. I was thinking of popping into Home Bargains, they usually have a good deal. Thomas: Home Bargains, yeah, cheap and cheerful.

Honestly, this thing’s got a mind of its own, hasn't it? Keep saying ‘In 200 yards, turn right onto a non-existent lane!’ I swear, the last time I trusted a satnav, it led me straight into a field full of sheep. Well, at least the sheep were entertained. You know, I read an article about how AI is being used to train autonomous drones for wildlife observation. Imagine flocks of little flying cameras – poetic, in a way, isn't it? Poetic and terrifying. I’d rather stick with my binoculars, thanks very much. And definitely not trust a machine to navigate me to a ceilidh! Speaking of which, are you sure we're on time? That band's supposed to start setting up in half an hour, and the venue's ages from here. Relax, love. We’re good. The satnav, despite its eccentricities, is telling me we’re just ten minutes behind schedule. Besides, I called Maisie earlier, and she said they’re running a bit late anyway - something about a last-minute shipment of tartan blankets. Apparently, it's crucial for the atmosphere. Tartan blankets? Good grief. Still, can't fault their dedication to authenticity. Remember old Mr. Henderson, down at the village hall, insisting on using actual heather for the decorations at the wedding last year? Nearly gave poor Emily a heart attack trying to sweep it all up. Oh, aye. That was a sight. Although, thinking about weddings… have you heard anything back from the photographer about Bethany’s wedding in September? She’s getting herself into a right state about it. Keeps saying she wants “atmospheric lighting” and “candid moments.” I chased him up yesterday. He promised to send over some sample shots. Honestly, these young people and their digital gizmos. My sister's wedding photos are all black and white and they are still beautiful. Something doesn't change and I like it. Digital's too quick, you know? No time to develop the emotion. That's it exactly. It’s the waiting, isn't it? That little pause to absorb the moment. Anyway, speaking of absorbing things… I’m famished. Have you got any of those ginger biscuits left? That dodgy shoulder of mine is playing up, and a bit of sugar usually helps. Aye, got a few. Though I warned you not to try that ridiculous Scandinavian lifting technique you saw on YouTube.

Honestly, did you see Chloe’s Instagram? She’s in Dubai – look at that brunch spread! Ridiculous. Dubai, huh? Always showing off. What's she doing there anyway? Apparently a “wellness retreat.” Probably just posing by a pool with a green smoothie. Anyway, what are we thinking for breakfast? I'm starving after battling those pigeons at the site. Right. Pigeons were a nightmare, weren't they? Landed right on my blueprints. I’ll get the coffees sorted. You want the usual? Please. And maybe a bacon bap? Extra bacon, if they'll let me. I need fuel. Two lattes and a bacon bap, please! So, speaking of battling… how's Mark holding up at Paragon? He sounded pretty down yesterday. Ugh, don’t even ask. He’s just… drowning. Apparently, the senior partner, Davies, is riding him relentless. All night emails, constant criticism... poor guy. Davies is a nightmare. Always has been. Remember that fiasco with the cladding report? Total overreaction. Mark’s got talent, he just needs to learn how to navigate Davies’ ego. Have you told him to document  everything ? Even the ridiculous demands? Yeah, I did. Said it’s CYA, cover your assets. He seemed to take that on board, but I worry he’s just pushing himself too hard. Reminds me a bit of when we were doing the Ruskin project – just fueled by caffeine and sheer terror. Oh god, don't remind me. That brief was insane. "Sustainable, brutalist, minimalist, and light-filled." Good luck with that! Still, we pulled it off, didn't we? Barely! Remember that week we were practically living in the studio? I think my hair turned grey overnight. Here's your fuel. So, back to Mark… maybe he should just start saying no? Delegating where he can? Easier said than done, I know. But he has to set some boundaries. Maybe have a chat with HR? Though, let's be honest, Paragon's HR is practically an extension of Davies’ ego. True. Okay, new tactic. Maybe subtly suggest he talk to Sarah from the London office? She’s ruthless, but she knows how to deal with Davies. Good idea. She's been there a while, hasn't she? It’s just… I wish he’d come to us sooner. We’re all in the same boat, and it shouldn’t be this isolating. We try. Anyway, let's change the subject.

Right, two sugars for you as always? And I’ve got those biscuits you like, the shortbread ones. Please! And yeah, shortbread's perfect. Thanks, Mum. This place smells lovely, like cinnamon and… relax, basically. Just trying to de-stress after that drive. Honestly, the A1 was a nightmare. Did you see the state of that queue near Stamford? Tell me about it! I left a bit earlier than usual because I knew it'd be busy, but I still ended up crawling along for about twenty minutes. Honestly, people have zero spatial awareness. Someone tried to merge into me when I was already practically on their bumper. Ugh, typical. It's the "assume everyone else is going slower than you" mentality. And then there’s the tailgating. I swear, some people think they're in a racing simulator. Exactly! It’s so stressful. I just put on my calming playlist and tried to breathe. Nearly honked, though. Nearly completely lost it. You and your calming playlists. What were you listening to? Loads of Sigrid. She’s so good. Makes everything a bit easier. So, what have you been up to? Anything exciting happening? Not particularly exciting. Work’s been busy, naturally. The Miller account is being particularly demanding this week. But Sarah invited us all out for dinner next Saturday. You free? Saturday? Let me check… Yeah, I think so! What’s she planning? Italian, at that new place, Bella Notte. Apparently, it’s really good. Thought we’d all go together, a bit of a proper catch-up. David's coming too, of course. Oh, brilliant! I haven’t seen Sarah in ages. Last time was at Christmas. Speaking of, did Gran send her Christmas card yet? Not yet, she’s been a bit… distracted lately. Apparently, she’s convinced the squirrels in her garden are planning a revolution. Oh, Gran! You know she's got a vivid imagination. Probably feeding them too many peanuts. Probably. She’s a soft touch when it comes to wildlife. Anyway, back to Saturday. Would you want me to book a table? Just for us initially, then I'll add David and Sarah on? Yes, please! That would be amazing. And tell Gran to keep an eye out for the squirrel uprising. Maybe invest in some tiny helmets. I will. Honestly, she’d probably knit them little uniforms. Right, your tea's ready.

Right, so I’ve got the first draft of the cover letter. Honestly, staring at a screen trying to make myself sound like a perfect candidate for a radio producer role is… exhausting. Tell me about it. I’ve been there. Send it over, let me have a look. You know I'm a bit of a wordsmith, even if I am just battling deadlines and soundbites all day. Okay, I’ll email it to you now. It’s mostly just regurgitating my experience, you know? Teaching languages, transferable skills and all that. But it feels a bit… vanilla. Vanilla’s fine as a starting point. It’s better than trying to be wildly creative and ending up sounding ridiculous. What’s the job description like? What are they  really  looking for? It's pretty comprehensive. They want someone with a flair for storytelling, excellent communication skills, experience with audio editing software – which I picked up doing student podcasts – and someone who can work independently but also collaborate with a team. Basically, the impossible. Sounds standard, doesn't it? The 'team player who can work independently' line is mandatory for everything these days. Don’t worry about the 'impossible' bit. Just highlight the bits where you  do  fit. So, about the transferable skills... you said you teach languages, right? Yeah, French and Spanish. Conversation-focused classes, lots of public speaking, adapting to different learning styles… Okay, there's gold in that. You’re essentially teaching people to communicate effectively, adapt their messaging to different audiences, and handle unexpected situations. That’s directly applicable to radio production. You’re crafting narratives, finding the right tone, and understanding what resonates with your listeners. Right! I hadn't quite framed it that way. I was thinking more about conjugation tables and subjunctive moods, not radio artistry. See? You're brilliant. Now, try plugging that in. Something like, "My experience facilitating dynamic and engaging language classes has honed my communication and adaptability skills, allowing me to effectively craft narratives and connect with diverse audiences – skills I believe would translate seamlessly to a radio production environment." Wow, that's… much better than what I had. It sounds a lot more confident. That’s because it  is  confident. You’ve got the skills; you just need to articulate them properly. What about your podcasting experience? They mentioned audio editing. I used Audacity mostly. Pretty basic, but I know how to record, edit, and mix audio.

Right, so let’s actually  nail  down a few actionable steps for this pottery thing, shall we? Just saying "I want to make mugs" isn't going to pay the bills, love. You’re absolutely right. You're always the practical one, aren’t you? I know, I know. It’s just… it feels so much more  me  than spreadsheets and marketing strategies ever did. And this house-sitting has given me a real taste for something creative. I’m really enjoying getting my hands dirty. And it’s a great skill to learn. Beautiful pieces. So, the initial hurdle, assuming the kiln rental works out – and we need to research that properly – is stock, right? Do we start with just a few designs, or a bigger launch? I was thinking small. A core range of mugs – classic shapes, a couple of nature-inspired patterns. Then, as I get better, I can introduce some more complex designs, maybe some bowls, plates… and then the custom commissions. That's where the real money will be, I reckon. Custom commissions. Okay. We need a pricing structure for those. And photographs, naturally. High-quality images are vital to selling anything online these days. We’ll need to invest in some good lighting too. Think about Etsy, initially? A simple online store? Etsy seems like a good starting point – low barrier to entry, lots of potential customers. But I also want something…mine. A proper website, eventually. Somewhere I have full control over the branding and the customer experience. Absolutely agreed. Etsy is a launchpad, not a destination. What about a name? Have you given any thought to the brand name? It’s surprisingly important. I’ve been toying with a few. "Clay & Bloom" – I like the contrast between the earthy clay and the blossoming of creativity. Or maybe something simpler, like "Dorchester Pottery" – playing on my roots. "Clay & Bloom" is lovely. It’s got a nice ring to it. Dorchester Pottery feels… a bit limiting, maybe? Plus, we’re not  in  Dorchester anymore. It’s about the creativity, the process, not just the location. Do a quick trademark search just to be safe, though. Always a good idea. Will do. And what about the legal side of things? Business registration, insurance… all that tedious stuff. Right. We need to set up a limited company, definitely. Protects your personal assets. I can look into that – I’ve got a good accountant.

Finn, stop running! Dinner's nearly over, and you’ll spill something. Honestly, he's got more energy than a Duracell battery. Zoom! I’m a race car! Vroom vroom! He certainly is a lively one, Eleanor. It’s wonderful to see him so full of beans. Though, you must be exhausted, dear. All that chasing! Exhausted is an understatement, Moira. I'm considering going on one of those juice cleanses just to get some energy back. But the thought of eating nothing but kale... ugh. Kale? Good heavens, woman! You need proper nourishment. Roast chicken, like we’ve just had, is what keeps you going. Builds character, it does. I remember back in the war… we’d practically kill for a decent piece of chicken. I know, George, but it’s not just the energy, it's... everything. The cost of everything, the struggle to keep up, you know? Especially with the housing situation in Cambridge. It's just ridiculous. It  is  dreadful, dear. Remember when I was teaching? We used to have proper classroom sizes. Now it’s twenty-five children crammed into a room meant for fifteen! And the school shortages are only getting worse. It’s not fair to the teachers, and certainly not fair to the children. Grandpa has a fluffy face! Like a bear! Indeed, Finn. I do rather. A distinguished beard, wouldn’t you say, Moira? I’ve been cultivating this for years. It started as a silly thing, a bet, but I rather like it now. Reminds me of Dickens. It suits you, George. Very impressive. Though, if I may say so, it does rather obscure your hearing! A small price to pay for literary gravitas, my dear. Though, it does make it difficult to hear Eleanor’s dietary woes. Oh, stop it. So, you know, I was thinking, maybe I should try that new app,  FitLife . It supposedly manages your meals and tracks your progress. My friend, Maria, said it's amazing. But I’m hopeless with computers. I can barely send an email. I'd be happy to help you with that, Eleanor. I’m quite handy with a computer these days, though it took me a while to figure it all out. You know, I remember when computers were just massive machines taking up entire rooms! Quite right. I used to publish novels entirely by hand, setting type myself. No computers then.

“Oh, this coffee is lovely, thanks, Jan. Feels ages since we properly chatted, doesn't it? How’s everything been?”      “It has, hasn’t it? Life seems to be moving at a million miles an hour these days. Everything's alright, you know, ticking along. The kids are all keeping me busy. How’s the marketing going? Still juggling everything yourself?”      “Pretty much! It’s a constant balance, that’s for sure. Proofreading's been quite steady though, which is a relief. I've actually landed a decent contract with a local publisher – a cookbook, believe it or not. Very different from the online stuff I usually do.”      “Oh, that’s brilliant, love. Well done! A cookbook, fancy that! Makes a change from all the online gubbins. Speaking of change, did you see that article about the new referendum they’re talking about? Seems like we're back to square one with Brexit.”      “Ugh, don’t even get me started! It’s just exhausting. Honestly, I try not to think about politics too much these days. My head aches enough already. What about you? Still enjoying the lunchtime supervisor role?”      “It’s alright. The kids are lovely, of course, but the staffroom’s a bit of a drama sometimes. You know how it is! I have been thinking about cutting back a bit though, as soon as young Tom's finished his football season. He’s getting so good, bless him.”      “He always was sporty. Remember at sixth form, he was practically living on the rugby field? Those were the days, weren't they? I haven’t thought about sixth form in ages!”      “Oh, my goodness, yes! Miss Davies’ history lessons – absolute torture! But good memories, I suppose. And remember that parking situation? The constant battle for a space… it was a nightmare getting a pass! Things haven't improved much I bet. Still the same chaos down at the local shops with people parking over the lines.”      “You're telling me! Speaking of driving, you wouldn’t believe the near miss I had last week. Some idiot pulled out right in front of me. Gave me a right fright.”      “Oh, goodness! Are you alright? It’s getting worse, isn't it? People just aren’t paying attention. It’s not like my knees are thanking me for gently braking either, mind.”      “Oh, your knees? How are they doing? Still giving you bother?”

Right, so, tell me more about this Twitter push for the Uni. You seemed really enthusiastic about it last week. Aye, I am! Honestly, I think we've been massively underutilizing it. It's not just a platform for shouting about open days, you know? It's a chance to engage, to build a community. I get that, in theory. But getting students and academics to actually  use  it properly… that's the challenge, isn’t it? My experience has been mostly shouting into the void. It took a bit of shifting the mindset, definitely. We started small. I ran a thread – a proper, lengthy, detailed thread – about the research being done by Professor MacIntyre on the impact of climate change on Scottish bee populations. I thought it would be a total snooze-fest. And…? It bloody went viral! Seriously, proper shares, retweets, engagement. People were asking questions, wanting to know more. It felt… useful, you know? Not just performative. Wow, that’s incredible. What do you think made the difference? Was it the topic itself? MacIntyre’s a big name, obviously. Partly, aye. MacIntyre’s respected. But I think it was the format. Laying it all out in clear, digestible chunks. And I made sure to tag relevant organisations and influencers. Proper hashtag research. Okay, that's good to know. We've been trying to encourage our lecturers to use LinkedIn more. I’m not entirely convinced it’s the right platform. Feels a bit… corporate, somehow. LinkedIn’s good for professional networking, definitely. But for reaching a broader audience, particularly younger ones? Twitter's still king. And TikTok, don't dismiss TikTok! We’re experimenting with short videos showcasing student life - lectures, labs, social events. TikTok! I was resistant to that one. Seems like a giant time sink. It can be. But even 30 seconds of a student explaining a complex scientific concept in a relatable way can do wonders for engagement. We had one video of a physics student demonstrating Bernoulli's principle using a hairdryer and a ping pong ball. It got thousands of views! Honestly? That sounds brilliant. We've been trying to do more video content, but it always feels so… polished. Overproduced. Exactly! Authenticity is key. People connect with real people showing real things. Students film it themselves, mostly. We just give them the guidelines, a brief. So less ‘professional communications team produced content’, more ‘genuine student perspective’?

Ugh, I am  done . Seriously, mentally and physically drained. That weekend at Sarah's was... a lot. Tell me about it. You looked like you needed a lie-down when you walked in. How was it, really? Beyond the general chaos of Sarah's parties, I mean. The chaos was palpable. Honestly, I spent most of Saturday trying to prevent Liam from starting a bonfire in the garden. He genuinely thought it would be a ‘festive touch.’ Liam. Of course he did. You’d think he'd learn after last summer's… incident. Exactly! And then Chloe spent the entire evening complaining about Mark. Again. Apparently, he didn't text her enough. Typical. She’ll be back with him next week, I reckon. They have a revolving door relationship, don’t they? Honestly! It's exhausting being around it. I swear, my eye roll muscles are cramping. What about you? How was your weekend? Must have been busy with work. It was. Two admissions on Saturday, and then a particularly difficult patient on Sunday. He was convinced he was being followed by pigeons. Oh, no. That sounds rough. Are you okay? Yeah, mostly. It’s emotionally draining, definitely. But it’s rewarding too, you know? Trying to make a difference, even a small one. Speaking of rewarding... I made a massive batch of that lentil soup you like. There's loads left. Seriously? You are a lifesaver! I was planning on just eating cereal for dinner. Nope. Soup and crusty bread. You deserve it after wrangling Liam and Chloe. So, what’s the plan for the week? Anything exciting? Not particularly. Just the usual grind. Trying to get this report finished. I'm starting to hate spreadsheets. They just… swirl. I hear you. Sometimes I wish I could just prescribe them a good dose of therapy. You should! I'd be a willing patient. Although, maybe if I just delete the whole thing and start again… Don't do that! You’ll end up more stressed. Actually, I was thinking… maybe we could get takeaway on Friday? Like that Thai place we both love? A proper de-stress evening. That sounds amazing! Yes, please. Do you think we should invite Maya and Ben? They seem a little down lately. Good idea. I'll text them. Just, tell them to brace themselves for another round of Chloe's relationship woes. Don't remind me.

Right, so, about Michael coming down… Have we sorted out the dates definitively this time? Last time it was a whole saga. Yes, Dad. He’s confirmed the 17th to the 21st. I double-checked with him this morning. He seems really keen to get away, actually. Said he needed a good dose of seaside air. Good. He needs it. Poor man. Still fretting over that whole business, isn't he? Aye. It’s a shame, really. He was a good worker, Michael was. Always reliable. Don't start feeling sorry for him, Dad. He made his choices. We just need to make sure he's comfortable while he's here. Did you manage to find that armchair you were looking at for the living room? The wider one? Not yet. Prices are scandalous, absolutely scandalous. I saw one yesterday, looked alright, but forty quid! For an armchair! Highway robbery, I tell you. You'll find something, love. Don’t worry. We’ve got a few days yet. How's the car holding up, Anon? Is it ready for the journey to pick him up? The car’s… well, it’s a car. . It's getting there. Managed to get a new tyre, though - needed it desperately. It was making the most awful noise. Sounded like it was trying to speak to me. Voices again, eh? You and those cars. Remember when your mum had that old Ford Fiesta? She swore it used to whisper to her. Oh, here we go. Another Mum story. It's a lovely story, love. Don’t be so dismissive. She loved that car. She used to say it felt like an extension of herself. She did. Everything was an extension of herself. You and Michael too. Always worrying about you both. Speaking of worrying, are you alright to cook on Saturday? I was thinking we could do that salmon you do so well. Michael loves it. Oh, darling, I’d be delighted. Salmon sounds lovely. And we have those new potatoes, the ones from Farmer Giles? They’d go perfectly. Right, salmon it is then. I’ll get the dill. Actually, I was thinking… should we get some of those new scallops from the fishmonger? They're saying they're exceptional this year. Bit of a treat for Michael. That sounds amazing, Dad! He’d really appreciate that. Though, be careful. He's a bit fussy about scallops.

Honestly, Arthur, I’m starting to think I’ll never get the hang of this Spanish. It’s just… relentless. Relentless is a good word, Margaret. Takes persistence, it does. You’re trying to cram too much in at once, aren’t you? Remember what I always said about surveying - break it down into manageable chunks. Manageable chunks? Arthur, the verb conjugations alone could fill the Albert Dock! Past perfect subjunctive… I can barely pronounce it, let alone understand when to use it. And don’t even get me started on the irregular verbs! Now, now. Don't get yourself agitated. You're attacking it like a school report. Think about the method. You're relying on that book, aren't you? All grammar and rules. Well, what else is there? Mrs. Davies at the community centre said this was the best method. Systematic, she called it. Going through everything step-by-step. Systematic’s fine, up to a point. But you need to  use  it, love. Immerse yourself. Remember when we watched that programme about Basque Country? All those people speaking both Basque and Castilian Spanish practically from birth. They pick it up naturally. Oh, yes, the one about the linguistic revival. Fascinating, really. But I’m not a child, Arthur. I can’t just absorb a language through osmosis. No, but you can get closer. Try watching some Spanish television, even if you only understand bits and pieces. Something lighthearted, you know? Maybe a comedy. Or listen to Spanish radio online. I tried that once. It was just a wall of noise. All those rapid-fire syllables... I felt like I’d swallowed a mouthful of gravel. It takes time. What about Duolingo? Are you using that? I hear it can be quite useful. I dabbled with Duolingo, but it just felt… frivolous. Like playing a game. I want to actually  learn  Spanish, not just collect little green birds. Well, there's an argument for gamification, you know. Keeps things engaging. And they do teach you some useful phrases. Think about Catalan. They have that whole structure, their own language completely integrated into Spanish life. It's amazing when you consider it. It is, isn’t it? A whole language interwoven with another. Makes me feel even more hopeless, to be honest. I’m trying to learn one, and they’re casually juggling two! Don't compare yourself to them, Margaret.

Right, so I think we’ve got all the big bills sorted. Just these miscellaneous documents left. Honestly, Dad, your filing system is… enthusiastic. Enthusiastic's one word for it, isn't it? Been building it up for thirty years, lad. You can't just toss it all out overnight. Though, I am glad you're here to help. My eyes aren't what they used to be. No worries. Found a couple of old flight confirmations from that trip to Spain. Remember that? Kelly Brook was on every magazine back then. Blimey, she hasn't aged a day. Kelly Brook! Still got it, she does. The papers are safe in here too. Can’t believe you remember that trip though. It was memorable. Especially the dodgy paella. So, these banking statements... looks like we need to scan these and send them to the accountant. Do you want to do that, or shall I? You do, love. My scanner's been acting up lately. Always throwing up some error message. I suspect it needs a good kick, but I'm not sure that’s the right approach. You’re better with the tech stuff. I can definitely handle the scanning. Just need to make sure I name the files properly so they don’t end up all jumbled. Need to be organized. Like with the corpus linguistics project at work. All those tagged words… Corpus linguistics? What's that then? Sounds complicated. Basically, it's analyzing huge amounts of text to see how language is actually used, not just how it  should  be used according to grammar books. It's fascinating, honestly. Sounds a bit like my job, really. Listening to what people actually  say  when they’re complaining about their internet bill, rather than what they  should  be saying. You could say that. Though, I doubt your data set is quite as large. Speaking of data, did you manage to sort out that password reset for your online banking? No, still battling with it. It’s changed the security questions, and I can’t for the life of me remember my first pet’s name. Was it Fluffy? Or Buster? I think it was Rufus, Dad. You’ve told me a million times. Don't let it become a digital hostage situation. They'll lock you out completely. You’re probably right. Right then, any chance you could have a go at it later?

Right, so I reckon we're getting low on petrol, aren't we? And this roundabout's a nightmare, honestly. Yeah, definitely getting low. And you're right about the roundabout, it's a complete free-for-all. Proper white-knuckle experience. Aye, it is! You'd think folk would learn to signal, wouldn't ya? Or give way! There was a right state earlier with that van cuttin' me off near the park. Honestly. People just seem to forget common courtesy on the roads. Do you want to stop at that Shell just up ahead? It usually has decent prices. Shell’s alright. Not as good as that independent station near Houghton, mind. They’ve got ridiculously cheap diesel, but it's a bit of a trek. I know, but we’re heading this direction anyway. Plus, the Shell has that little coffee shop. Fancy a latte? Oh, that does sound good, actually. Driving’s makin’ me peckish. You know, I saw a bunch of bikers earlier, roaring down the A1. Did you? Were they a group? Aye, a right noisy bunch! All shiny bikes and leather jackets. Looked like they were heading for a meet somewhere. Always makes you wonder where they're going, doesn't it? Proper sense of freedom, I suppose. Though terrifying to be behind one when they brake suddenly. Aye, tell me about it! I nearly had a heart attack when one pulled out right in front of me on the way to see Gran last week. Gave me a right fright. Reckon they think they own the road, some of ‘em. You’re probably right. Though, some of them are genuinely skilled riders. It's a bit of an art, I suppose. Skill or not, I wouldn’t trust ‘em! Give me a nice, sensible family car any day. Less… adrenaline-inducing. Agreed. Although, they do look rather cool, I must admit. Especially when they’re all lined up outside a pub. Cool and loud, that’s about it. Right, petrol station then? Before I get any more hungry. Yeah, let’s do it. And grab that latte. Keeps us both awake on this route. You driving back, or do you want me to take over? I'll drive back, thanks. I need the exercise, even if it  is  just wrestling with roundabouts and dodging bikers! Plus, you looked a bit tired earlier. Fair enough.

Right then, so Mr. Davies – what did you think of the coaching session today? Did you manage to nail that backhand slice he was on about? It was alright, Mum. He kept saying I was ‘over-rotating’ again. Honestly, it sounds like a medical condition, not a tennis problem. Over-rotating, eh? Classic. That's what they all say. It's about finding the sweet spot, isn’t it? Just a little adjustment. You’re putting too much effort in, lad. Relax your shoulders. He’s probably right, love. Remember when I was trying to learn that serve from Kevin at the club? I was swinging for the fences every time! Ended up just hitting it into the net. Yeah, well, Kevin’s probably still playing at a higher level than me. He's been at it for ages. Don’t be daft. You’ve got potential. You just need to be consistent. Watch some replays of Djokovic. Dreadful weather, isn't it? Just relentless. Though, I suppose it  is  Somerset. One shouldn’t expect anything else. You’re telling me. So much time and energy… for something that feels like a David and Goliath battle.

Speaker_1 : "Right, let’s have a proper look through this then, Mary. It’s been sitting here gathering dust. Look at this little terror – Daniel at his third birthday party. Remember that clown?" Right, I think we’ve demolished most of the roast! How’s the trifle looking? I know you two always loved it. Lovely, Sarah, absolutely lovely. You always did make a cracking trifle. So, anything interesting on the telly this morning? Not the news, I've had enough of that to last a lifetime. They were showing that bird documentary. The puffins. You should get it looked at soon, before it becomes a full-blown disaster. I remember my Nana's car doing that – she ignored it for months and ended up needing a whole new engine!      Speaking of disasters, I’m still mortified about that email I sent to the client last week. You know, the one where I accidentally called them ‘Dear Derek’ instead of ‘Dear David’?      Oh, Imogen! Maybe we could convince Mum to come with us somewhere. She's never been abroad, has she? Abroad… pugs… warm… Mum? Are you alright? You drifted off there for a moment. She’s probably thinking about Buster. She misses him terribly. Poor thing. He was a character. Remember how he used to steal socks and hide them under the sofa? Oh my goodness, yes! A pug sock hoard! You should’ve posted that on social media.

Right, so I’m thinking chicken tagine tonight. Got all the spices, just need to get the chicken browned off properly. You reckon too much ginger’s a bad thing? Did you finally book that tattoo appointment? Almost! Matty at Red Line said he could squeeze me in next week. I’m still agonising over the actual design though. Maybe something small on my wrist? A little line constellation? Stupid, innit? Not stupid at all. Elegant, actually. It sounds lovely. Though, do consider placement. Wrists can fade a bit quicker. Remember Aunt Carol's rose? Barely visible now. Yeah, good point. Maybe my arm then. Less sun exposure. Anyway, what are you up to this weekend? Anything exciting planned? Just catching up on edits, mostly. That new author, Eleanor Finch, is proving…challenging. So many exclamation points! And the interns are proving even more challenging than her prose. Honestly, they’re utterly useless. Right, just needs a little more…tarragon, I think. Honestly, this recipe is a bit vague. "A sprinkle of tarragon." A sprinkle to  whom ?      You and your precision. Honestly, this place is surprisingly busy for a Monday morning. You’d think everyone would be dreading the week. Well, they've probably already got their workout in. They're now analysing films through a TikTok lens. Apparently, 'Barbie' was a really deep commentary on… something. I’m still trying to figure out what. Did you see it? I did! With the kids. Honestly, I went in expecting pink fluff and came out… questioning everything. Margot Robbie was incredible, though. It’s that kind of dedication that elevates a film. Speaking of commitment, did you hear about… …that rumour about Harry and Meghan? Something about a split? Oh, here we go. The royal gossip machine. Honestly, I’m not surprised. You can't fake that kind of pressure. And the media… relentless. It's probably manufactured anyway, isn't it? Just another distraction. That's what I thought. It all feels a bit… convenient, doesn't it? You know, like someone’s orchestrating it. It's like the whole thing with the weather. I’ve been reading up on geoengineering and… Whoa, slow down! Geoengineering? You've gone full conspiracy theorist on me. Last time I saw you, you were worried about rogue pigeons. It's not  rogue  pigeons, it's… well, it’s the patterns they fly in! And look, I'm just saying, the evidence is compelling. They're spraying stuff into the atmosphere… Right. He’s talking about selling his car to fund his collection.

Dad, are we nearly there yet? This journey is taking forever! Nowt ever feels like it’s 'nearly' when you’re in a car with a teenager, love. It’s a journey, not a sprint. Look out the window, eh? See that field? Full o’ buttercups. Yeah, yellow. Everything’s either green or yellow, isn’t it? A bit boring. I wish I’d brought a good book. You could’ve brought Wizard of Oz. I put it in the bag. Do I have to read that? I've seen the film like a million times. It’s a classic, lass! And it’s got Dorothy, and a lion, and a tin man… Loads of good stuff. Reminds me of fairy tales, doesn't it? All about finding your way home. Sort of. I guess. Speaking of finding ways, are you sure you’re going the right way? It feels like we’ve been driving through fields forever. Is it like, Jamaica Inn fields? Aye, it could be. Reminds me of that place. Bit bleak up there, innit? Dodgy looking smugglers! Read a Sherlock Holmes story set there once. Proper creepy. Although, I wouldn’t put it past someone. You know, my old geography teacher, she could speak a bit of French. Used to try and teach us some on Fridays. I’m hopeless at languages. I can barely remember the French words for 'cat'. Never mind, you’re good at other things. You're a good artist. Where have you put that sketchbook? Why haven’t you been drawing all these lovely hedges? I was on my phone. Sorry. Got a text from Chloe. She's expecting loads of photos from the beach. Chloe, eh? Always on that phone. Right, let's check the fuel gauge. Don't want to be stuck in the middle of nowhere.

Speaker_1 : Right, so who’s admitting to switching the cards again? Finn, you’ve got that look about you. Speaker_3 : Me? I’m just trying to strategize! Right, that’s the last of the boxes from the flat. Feeling utterly wrecked, Mum. Jet lag is  real . Oh, love, you look it. Sit down, sit down. I’ve made you a proper Sunday roast. Perfect for my plants. Speaking of, are you still thinking about selling your jewellery collection? You mentioned it last time I was down. I am. It's just… a lot of memories attached to it. Your father gave me most of it. Still, need to downsize, don't I? And the money would be handy for getting the bathroom done in the new place. Though, goodness, I’m not sure I’m ready to part with that turquoise necklace. I understand. But think of the new bathroom! You deserve a nice, modern bathroom. Although, on a slightly different note… have you been hearing from Sarah and Ben?

Aye, look at that fella's clematis. Proper jungle he’s got there. Wish mine were doing that well. They’re just…limping along, poor things. Yeah, they’re tricky, aren't they? So, did you see anything about the NHS in the news today? It’s getting worse, isn’t it? Terrible, isn’t it? My cousin’s been waiting months for a scan. Months! It’s just… heartbreaking to hear. People were queuing for ages just to get a few litres. It's crazy, isn’t it? They said it was a temporary shortage, but I reckon it's going to be a problem for a while.

- Chloe      - Freya      - Maisie      - Liv      …and then the lecturer was like, “Well, clearly it’s a representation of patriarchal oppression!” Honestly, I nearly choked on my tea. This is just… incredible, isn’t it? The light is unbelievable. It is lovely. Though I’m having terrible signal out here. Oh god, the spiritualism phase. I’ve seen that before. Exactly. So I started replying to her messages later and later.

That pasta was incredible, Grandma. Seriously, you've outdone yourself. Nonsense, darling. It’s just a simple recipe. But you know, sometimes the simplest things are the best. So, tell me, how's university going? Still drowning in essays, I presume? Pretty much. This term feels particularly intense. I’ve got a massive presentation on post-war British art coming up. Post-war? Oh, that’s interesting. You know, I was quite active in the art scene then. Lot of vibrant experimentation happening. Did you have to read anything about, oh, I don't know, Henry Moore? A sense of resilience, of making something beautiful from very little. Speaking of making something beautiful... I’m thinking of starting a new series. Landscapes, I think. It's been too long since I saw the Ligurian Sea. Remember when your grandfather and I used to take that little Fiat down there? The lemon groves... the smell… I do. Dad’s told me stories. He says you'd spend hours sketching the fishermen and the boats. He exaggerates! But he’s right, I did love sketching. How is your brother doing? Last I heard, he was considering going to that climbing course in Scotland. He’s signed up! Leaves next week, actually. Says he's terrified but also really excited. It's like painting, in a way, isn't it? Stepping outside your comfort zone. Taking a risk. I suppose it is. Speaking of books, I just finished ‘Lincoln in the Bardo’ by George Saunders. Have you read it? Saunders? No. What's it about? It's… difficult to explain. It’s a novel set in a graveyard, narrated by ghosts. It’s really experimental, stream of consciousness, very moving.

Right then, nearly halfway through this leg, I think. How’s your arm feeling? Still achey from yesterday’s…enthusiastic gym session? A little bit, yeah. Proper sore. Though I suspect my engaging mostly involves desperately trying to remember the right conjugation of a verb. With increasingly confused faces staring back at me. You’re brilliant at it, honestly. You just have... a presence. A very English presence. Like you’ve wandered off the set of a period drama and ended up teaching teenagers about modal verbs. That’s probably not far off the truth. You’d think people would focus on your competence, rather than…your gender. Exactly! It's like, I’ve got a Master's degree in TEFL and I’m overqualified by a mile, but apparently, my womanhood makes me somehow less capable. It’s just wear and tear, isn’t it? All that constant quiet questioning. You have to learn to brush it off. Though easier said than done. I guess. Sometimes I swear it’s worse in this country. Back home, people are a bit more… honest, maybe. A bit less subtle about their prejudices. It’s just… different. Different shades of the same awful colour, probably.
