This coffee is…adequate. Not quite the robust Italian blend I’m accustomed to, you know? Ah, you’re always dreaming of Italy, David. Tredegar coffee will never quite measure up, will it? Though, I must say, it’s a welcome pick-me-up after that funding meeting. Don’t even mention it, Rhys. They’re being utterly glacial about the research project. Five years we’ve been meticulously gathering data on ancient Egyptian irrigation techniques, and they’re quibbling over a measly ten thousand pounds! Ten grand? That's daylight robbery! What are they saying? The proposal isn't robust enough? Something along those lines. Apparently, the methodology needs “further clarification.” As if they even read the blasted thing! It's been peer-reviewed twice! I swear, some days I feel younger than my students just wrestling with this bureaucratic nonsense. Tell me about it! I've been battling with the university's facilities department for weeks now about redecorating my office. They’ve approved the paint colour – a calming shade of beige – but won't let me have the bookshelf I requested. Apparently, it’s a “structural integrity concern.” A bookshelf? Rhys, you're pulling my leg. I wish I were! Apparently, they're worried it'll fall and crush someone. I told them I’d personally guarantee its safety, but to no avail. It's rather depressing, having to teach surrounded by these drab, blank walls. Makes me feel like I'm lecturing in a waiting room. Well, at least you’re getting a fresh coat of beige. My wife insists we repaint the kitchen. Wants a sort of… pistachio green. Pistachio green? Bit bold, isn’t it? You have no idea! I argued for a subtle olive, something dignified, but she's adamant. Says it’ll brighten the space. I suspect she just liked the name. "Pistachio." It sounds vaguely Mediterranean, doesn’t it? Like a fancy Italian snack. You're doomed, my friend. The wives always win. It’s a universal truth, you know. Speaking of universal truths, have you been following the news about that water company being fined again? Honestly, you’d think they’d learn. Disgraceful. Absolutely disgraceful. They’re charging us exorbitant rates and providing water that tastes like…well, let’s just say I don’t trust it. I’ve been using a filter. Reminds me of Cairo, actually. Always had to filter the water there.

Right, operation Lego sort is a go! Leo, stop trying to eat the yellow brick, please. It’s yellow like sunshine! Sunshine doesn't taste very good, sweetheart. It's for building, remember? Like a castle! Or… a spaceship. Spaceship! Pew pew! Exactly! Now, you two have been building… abstract masterpieces, let's say. But we need to actually sort them. Reds with reds, blues with blues, greens with… well, you get the idea. Can we build a dragon first? We can build a dragon  after  we sort. Promise. Then the dragon can guard our perfectly sorted Lego. Think of it – a very organised dragon. Can it breathe fire? It can breathe fire… made of red Lego bricks! See? Practical. Right, who wants to start with the blue ones? Me! Blue is my favourite colour! Like Hermione’s robes. That’s right! Hermione’s brilliant. Remember when she used the Time-Turner in Harry Potter? That was clever. Bart Simpson! Bart Simpson? Where did that come from? He's funny! He says "Eat my shorts!" He does, doesn't he? Bart’s a classic. But right now, Bart needs to help with the Lego. After that we can watch a Simpsons episode. Deal? Deal! Deal! Ninja Turtles! Ninja Turtles? Okay, okay. After the Lego, and  maybe  after the Simpsons, we could even think about the cinema. They’re showing a new TMNT movie, aren’t they? Yeah! Leonardo's the best! Raphael! He’s got a big sword! Everyone has their favourite. You know, my Granny keeps saying we should come and stay with her more. She’s been doing a lot of renovations. Apparently, the kitchen is practically unrecognisable. Granny’s kitchen is yucky! It’s getting better, sweetie. Much better. She's trying to make it more modern. We should take you both to see it properly. Can we have Easter chocolate there? Granny has chocolate! I'm sure Granny will have chocolate. She always does. Right, focus! Lego first. Red ones, Leo. I found a purple one! Is purple a colour? It is! It's a very important colour. Put it with the blues, it’ll look fantastic. Now, who's ready to be a Lego master sorter? Me! Pew pew! That’s the spirit. See? Organised dragons are much easier to build when you have sorted Lego. And a well-sorted life is a happy life, right?

Oh my god, it’s so good to be back! This flat feels…right. Even with the mountain of washing I'm about to face. You’re back! Welcome home! Give us a hug! How was Greece? Seriously, tell me  everything . You look exhausted, though. Plane delayed? Exhausted is an understatement. The flight was fine, but the transfer…don’t even get me started. Lost luggage for a couple of hours, then a twenty-minute queue for a taxi. But Greece itself was amazing! Beautiful. And the food…oh, the food! I missed you tons. And I totally raided your Greek yogurt supply while you were gone. Sorry, not sorry. You absolute menace. I bought that especially for my breakfasts, you know! Did you at least try to make moussaka? Almost! I found a recipe, but then remembered I didn't own a potato peeler. It's a crisis, I tell you. Anyway, what did you actually  do ? Beaches, cocktails…? Did you meet a handsome Greek fisherman? Very funny. I did lots of beaches, lots of cocktails. And the sunsets... seriously breathtaking. Met a few nice people, nothing exciting on the fisherman front, though. Though there  was  this one guy… Ooh, spill! What was he like? Give me all the details! Was he rugged and windswept? Did he have a boat? He was…okay. A bit too into ancient Greek mythology for my liking, if I'm honest. Spent the entire afternoon explaining the significance of Poseidon to me. I just wanted to lie on the beach and read a book! Sounds utterly dreadful. So, no follow-up then? Nope. I think my interest peaked after he tried to compare me to Aphrodite. Bit much, isn’t it? How was  your  week? Actually, work-wise… it must have been manic with you being short-staffed. Don’t even ask. It was relentless. Had a few really tough cases, but thankfully nothing too major. It's nice to be home and just…decompress, you know? Did Sarah text you while I was here? She said she wanted to grab brunch next week. Yes, I got her message! I said next Wednesday looked good. I’ll send her a quick reply now. Are you free for dinner tonight? I’m thinking of ordering a takeaway – I’m not really in the mood to cook after that travel chaos. Perfect! I’m starving. Pizza? Or should we be adventurous?

Right then, so the plumber’s coming on Thursday afternoon. Did you remember to clear a bit of space in the downstairs loo for him, Liam? Aye, Mum. Moved all the bath bombs and stuff. Is he good? Last one left a right mess. Apparently, he’s recommended by Mrs. Higgins next door. She swears by him. Says he’s reliable and doesn’t try to fleece you. That’s all I ask. Fleece you? Back in my day, you were lucky if they turned up at all. Remember your grandad, Elsie? Tried to fix the tap once himself. Flooded the kitchen! Aye, that I did. Nearly drowned the cat! Your mother had a right go at me for that one. He did, didn't he? Honestly, Dad, you and your DIY attempts. Makes me worry about you two managing on your own. We’re fine, lass. We’ve got each other. And I still remember how to boil a kettle, thank you very much. Gran, you boiled the kettle the other day and set off the smoke alarm. Well, it was a new kettle! Didn't know it was that powerful. Honestly, you two are a pair. Liam, have you finished that essay yet? The one on the Tudors? Nearly. Just need to write the conclusion. It’s rubbish, though. I can’t think of anything clever to say. Don’t be daft. You’ll think of something. Just summarise your main points. What was the most interesting thing you learned? Probably how many wives Henry VIII had. It’s mental, isn’t it? Seven wives he had. That’s a lot of bother for one man. Aye, and all that chopping off of heads. Not a good look, that. Though I always thought Anne Boleyn was quite stylish. See? Even Gran’s got an opinion on royal history. Speaking of heads, did you hear that joke? Oh, here we go. What do you call a sad strawberry? I don't know, Mum. What? A blueberry! That’s awful. That's a good one! A right good one! You haven’t changed a bit, Margaret. Still telling those silly jokes. Well, someone has to keep things lighthearted. Now, dinner's nearly ready. Liam, could you set the table, love? And Dad, could you pop the kettle on for a brew? Kettle’s on now, lass. Careful though, don’t want to set off any alarms!

Right, so, did you two enjoy  Peter Pan  this afternoon? Big film night, wasn’t it? Yes! Tinkerbell was brilliant! She flew! I liked the pirates! Captain Hook was really scary!  Growls  He was a bit scary, wasn’t he? But Peter Pan was braver, wasn’t he? Did you see how he fought them off? He had a sword! And he could fly too! Like Tinkerbell! That's right. Although, Tinkerbell's magic is a bit different, isn't it? She uses fairy dust. Did you know they have a special ward at Great Ormond Street for children with illnesses? And sometimes, they decorate it to look like Neverland, so the kids can feel a bit like they’re in the film. Really? Yeah. They try to make them feel a little bit magic, you know? Like Tinkerbell is looking after them. It’s really clever. They do amazing things there. Does Tinkerbell  really  help the children? Well, not  really  really. But the people at Great Ormond Street do, and they work so hard. Sometimes when you donate to help them, they can buy special toys and things to make the children feel better. Can we give them some toys? That’s a wonderful idea, darling. We can definitely talk about that. Maybe we could even draw some pictures for them, too. What would you draw? A pirate ship! With lots of pirates! I’ll draw Tinkerbell! With lots of fairy dust!  Sprinkles imaginary fairy dust . Perfect. Now, did you notice how they made the Lost Boys in the film? They all looked so different, but they were still friends. It's good to have friends, isn't it? Yes! You’re my friend, Mummy! And me! I’m your friend too! You are the very best friends a mummy could ask for. Now, supper’s almost ready, and then we can have a little chat about how Peter Pan always found a way to go home, even though Neverland was so exciting. It’s important to remember where you come from, you know? Even if you have adventures. Where do we come from, Mummy? We come from Comberton, sweetheart. And this kitchen. And we come from love and lots of cuddles. Now, who wants spaghetti? Me! Pirates like spaghetti! Of course they do. Right then, let's get this spaghetti on the table! I'll get the plates. Can we watch Tinkerbell again tomorrow?

Right, well, that’s us then, isn't it? Another trip done. Honestly, these Devon roads… they’re a character in themselves, aren’t they? Each little village, each bend… reminds you of something. They really do. Though I'm glad they're behind us now. My eyelids were starting to droop. That early start really took it out of me. Teaching Year 3 is demanding enough without running on fumes. You’re being modest, love. You are brilliant with those little ones. Remember when we lived in that cottage near Bovey Tracey? You used to complain about the commute then. At least now you’re closer to the school. That's true. Though that cottage  was  lovely. Remember the garden? We spent ages trying to get the roses to bloom properly. Roses! You were obsessed. And the hills! Remember how steep the drive was? Nearly broke my back carrying the shopping up there. I'm quite glad we don't live back in that area, as its all changed. It has. They've built a load of new houses, haven't they? It’s not the same. Still, we had some good times there. What about that little place we rented in Taunton for a few months, though? That was a different kettle of fish altogether. Oh god, Taunton! The rain! It rained practically every day. And that tiny kitchen... And the estate agent insisted it was "a charming, bijou property." Charming! Bijou! It was cramped! Still, it was a change of scenery. And we managed to find a lovely pub down the road. Good food too. Speaking of changes though, how's the house-warming party planning going? Have you sorted out the guest list yet? It's… a work in progress. I’m trying to keep it manageable. I don't want it to be chaotic. I've sent out the invitations – mostly teachers and family, of course. And a few of the parents from school. Don’t forget Auntie Maureen. She’ll want to bring her famous fruitcake. Oh dear. That fruitcake’s a weapon, isn't it? Don't let her near the children with that thing. Noted! And I was thinking of putting up some fairy lights in the garden. Make it a bit more festive. Sounds lovely. Have you thought about Christmas yet? It’ll be your first Christmas in the new house. We should all spend it together, shouldn’t we?

Speaker_1 :   A woman in her late 70s, dressed in practical but stylish clothing, a faint scent of lavender about her.     Speaker_2 :   A man in his early 80s, wearing a well-worn fleece and a flat cap.        Arthur:   Afternoon. Blimey, busy day, isn't it? Trackwork’s a right bother.   Eleanor:   Indeed, it is. Disruptive, isn't it? Though a necessary evil, I suppose. Are you involved in the working party?   Arthur:   Involved, aye. More of a… lookout, really. Making sure nobody wanders onto the line. Not as fit as I used to be. Used to be a dab hand at this sort of thing back in my Nationwide days, you know. So many buildings to look after.   Eleanor:   A very important role. Keeping things safe. It’s surprising how casually people can disregard safety procedures. I was reading an article the other day about the benefits of a good Swedish massage. Helps release tension, apparently. Might do you some good after all this exertion.   Arthur:   Massage, eh? My wife, Doris, she used to try and rub my shoulders. Never quite had the know-how, though. She’s in a hospice now, you see. Not long, sadly.   Eleanor:   Oh, dear. I am so very sorry to hear that. A difficult time.   Arthur:   Aye, it is. We've been married over sixty years. Never thought I’d face it without her. Makes you realise how precious every moment is. Did you know Doris was a nursery nurse? Proper dedication she had, those little ones adored her. Wonderful with children.   Eleanor:   That’s lovely. Investing in early childhood education… it’s essential, isn’t it? Sets them up for life. Though I do worry sometimes about the terminology. "Learning outcomes" and all that. It's lost the joy of simply  playing .   Arthur:   They’re always changing things, aren’t they? Back in my day, it was just “let them have fun and learn a bit.” Progress, they call it. I’ve never quite understood it. Though Doris always said women had to fight harder for equality in her day when she was working. A constant battle, she said.   Eleanor:   Absolutely. It's a battle that continues, sadly. Though it’s heartening to see more women taking leadership roles. I’m involved in the Women’s Engineering Event next year. It's a fantastic initiative to encourage more girls to pursue STEM careers.   Arthur:   Engineering, eh?

Right, so I was looking at flights again, Mum. And EasyJet have got some really good deals to Malaga for mid-September. Malaga, lovely! Haven't been there in years. Is that where you wanted to go? You were dithering between Spain and Portugal, weren't you? I know, I know. But the flights to Portugal were significantly more expensive. Malaga just seems the easiest and most budget-friendly option at the moment. And the weather’s supposed to be gorgeous still. Well, that’s sensible, darling. Don’t want to be freezing! What’s the accommodation looking like? Have you found somewhere nice? I’m trying to! There are loads of apartments on Airbnb, but honestly, some of them look… dodgy. Like, single lightbulbs and mismatched furniture. You know the sort. I want somewhere that feels reasonably comfortable for a week. Well, you don’t want to be slumming it, do you? Especially on a holiday. Have you looked at those holiday rental companies, like Sykes Cottages or something? They're usually a bit pricier, but generally, you get what you pay for. I did have a quick look, but they were a bit out of my price range. I was hoping to keep the whole thing under £800, flights and accommodation combined. £800, for a week in Spain? That’s… ambitious, but not impossible. Especially if you're willing to be a bit flexible on the location. Don't need to be right on the beach, do you? A little further inland might be cheaper. No, I’m not that bothered about being right on the beach. A short bus ride is fine. I was thinking somewhere near Torremolinos, maybe? It seems to have a decent amount of things to do. Torremolinos is alright, a bit touristy, perhaps. But a good base. You could get a bus to Malaga city itself and explore. Have you looked at Nerja? I’ve heard good things. Nerja? I’ll have a look. Is it pretty? It’s very pretty! Whitewashed houses, lovely views of the sea, a really nice atmosphere. It’s not as manic as some of the other resorts. Just lovely. It might take a bit more travelling to get around, but it's worth it. Okay, I’ll have a proper search for Nerja. And maybe check out those holiday rental companies again. Do you think I should book something soon, or wait a bit longer in case the prices drop?

Right, so, transfer went through alright, then? The one to Mum for the deposit?      Yes, Liam. Confirmed. She sent a screenshot of her account. Said she’s already been looking at a couple of places.      Good, good. Just wanted to double check. She’ll be buzzing, won't she? Finally getting out of that flat.      Absolutely. She deserves it. It was always a bit cramped, especially with the kids getting bigger. Speaking of which, have you heard from your sister lately?      Just a quick text yesterday. Said Maisie's soccer team won their tournament. Proper proud of her, she apparently scored two goals.      That’s fantastic! She's got some serious talent. Remember when she used to just kick the ball into the flowerbeds?      How could I forget? Mum nearly had a heart attack. Anyway, back to this transfer... I’m just feeling a bit worried about money, you know? Course fees are coming up again.      I understand. Look, let's not dwell on it. Focus on the positives. Your degree’s valuable, and you’ve got skills. Speaking of skills, how's that coding course going?      It's alright, it's alright. It’s a bit of a slog sometimes, to be honest. The algorithms are killing me. But I’m sticking with it. You know I always finish what I start.      That's the spirit. And it’s good for your CV. Regarding my work, things are hectic as usual. We’re trying to finalize the quarterly reports and my boss got on my back this morning. Said I wasn't ensuring the teams were hitting their targets.      Really? That's rough. You're working your socks off, aren’t you? It's not your fault if the team's struggling.      I know, but you have to manage expectations, don't you? Still, at least it's steady work. I saw on the news this morning that that footballer, Rashford, he's trying to get free school meals extended over the holidays again.      Massive respect for him, that lad. Proper using his platform for good. Heard he's been doing a lot of charity work too. He’s a good role model.      He is. It’s refreshing to see a celebrity who actually cares. I read an article about Rihanna, too. Apparently, she’s expanding her school in Barbados – the one she funded years ago.      Good on her! She never forgets her roots, does she?

Speaker_1 :   Lovely tea, Margaret. Proper brew, this. Bit stronger than yours, mind.   Speaker_2 :   Well, you always say that, Arthur. It’s just a bit of Yorkshire Gold! Now, Graham, are you still picking up alright? You’re looking a bit blurry there.   Speaker_3 :   Yeah, sounds fine, Margaret. Bit patchy, mind you – internet's playing up again. Just a tad pixelated, but can hear you lot loud and clear. So, Arthur, you were just saying? Something about globes, wasn’t it?      Aye, globes. Been looking at this old thing I got back from the attic. Remember it, Margaret? Big, dusty thing. Showed all the British Empire. Shows how things’ve changed, don’t it?      Oh, I do! You used to spend hours pointing at places, claiming you’d been there, even though you'd never left Costessey!      Had a bit of an imagination, I did. Always wanted to go. Remember reading about youth hostels in Switzerland, back in the day? Used to dream of hiking in the Alps. Never happened though, did it?      My lad did the Alps, years ago. Part of a school geography project. Had to document the local flora and fauna. Said it was brilliant, though a bit pricey. He was forever moaning about the cost of the transport.      School projects these days are so complicated. When I was helping my little ones with history, it was just memorizing dates! My granddaughter's doing one on the London Underground – the engineering, the history... It's a beast.      The 'Tube'. Always thought it a bit of a marvel, that system. Imagine digging all that! Never been on it myself, of course. Just read about it.      It is quite something, Arthur. Honestly, it's a subterranean city down there. Speaking of travel, Margaret, how's the garden looking? You were saying about the roses?      They’re coming along nicely, thank you. Bit of a battle with the aphids, but I’m winning. I planted some lavender, too. Smells wonderful. Just need to prune the wisteria before it takes over the whole back garden.      Lavender… reminds me of my mother's garden. She had a right good patch of it. Strong smell, that.      My wife's been trying to get me into gardening. Says I need to get out more. I spend most evenings marking essays or watching telly. Speaking of which, did you see that new detective show on Sunday? Dreadful, really.

Honestly, EasyJet’s website is having a right laugh. Every time I refresh, the prices change. It's like they're deliberately messing with us. Tell me about it! I spent a good half an hour last night trying to get flights to Prague, and they kept jumping up. It's ridiculous. Did you manage to find anything decent for Barcelona? Not really. I've found flights for around £180 return, but they're at absolutely awful times. Like, really early morning departures, which are never fun after a late night. And the return is at 8pm on a Sunday. Not ideal. Ugh, yeah, those times are grim. I’m trying to be patient and wait for a dip, but I'm a bit worried they’ll just keep going up. Should we just bite the bullet and book now, even if it's a bit pricey? I'm tempted. I’ve set up a price alert though, so hopefully, I'll get a notification if anything drops. It's just… I'm trying to keep it under £150 if possible. Fancy a refill? Anon’s made loads of this butternut squash lasagne. Please! I'm starving after lugging myself and my suitcase up three flights of stairs. This is delicious by the way, Anon’s a genius. Seriously, I should ask her for the recipe. She wouldn’t give it away! She’s notoriously secretive about her cooking. Last Christmas, she wouldn't share her stuffing recipe. Said it was "a family secret." Honestly! Some people. So, Barcelona then? Are you still definite on the dates? Yeah, thinking the 17th to the 20th. Got a rough itinerary planned – Park Güell, Sagrada Familia, wander down Las Ramblas… you know, the usual touristy stuff. Sounds amazing! I’m just craving some good tapas already. I'm also trying to figure out my work holiday booking. It's a nightmare. Apparently, everyone wants to go in August. Tell me about it! That’s always the case. You'll have to fight for it. Maybe try putting in a request for something a bit less popular, like… November? November in London? No thank you! I'd rather take my chances in the August scrum. I've been eyeing up a pottery class, actually. Something creative to do while I'm there. Ooh, that's a good idea! I might look into that too.

Lovely bit of sunshine we’re having, eh? Wouldn’t have believed it after that deluge last week. It is nice. Though I’m bracing myself for more rain next week. The forecasts are never reliable, are they? Never! They said last week would be glorious, and we got flooded out. Honestly, it’s like they just pluck numbers out of thin air. Remember that badger that got stuck in Mrs. Henderson's shed last summer? Weather was supposed to be perfect. Torrential rain instead. Badgers are crafty creatures. Always have been. Mind you, I saw a fox the other day, bold as brass, rooting through my bins. Cheeky little blighter. Wildlife's getting braver, isn’t it? Probably because people are leaving more food out. Speaking of leaving things out, have you seen the price of bread at Sainsbury's lately? It's scandalous! Nearly four pounds for a loaf. I’m sticking to Aldi, thank you very much. Aldi's the way to go. Used to be embarrassed to shop there, but now… well, everyone’s struggling. The bank’s been on to me again, wanting to review my overdraft. Said interest rates are going up. Oh, Dad, that's awful! Are you sure you need an overdraft? Have you looked at switching banks? Some offer better deals, especially with loyalty schemes. Loyalty schemes? Trying to be loyal to a bank is like sticking with a terrible mobile phone provider! They’ll rip you off if they can get away with it. I switched to that new one, LycaMobile, and it’s brilliant. Cheaper calls, more data… LycaMobile, you say? Might have to look into that. I’m still with Orange, stubborn as an ox, I am. Can’t be bothered to change. Stubbornness will cost you, Dad. It really does. But tell me, are you still feeling alright? You mentioned your knee was giving you trouble last time I saw you. It’s just a bit of stiffness. Nothing to worry about. Just getting old, you know? The joints start to creak. Old? We’re all getting old! Though I’m trying to fight it. Started doing Tai Chi with the ladies down the community centre. Helps with the stiffness, apparently. That’s brilliant, Mum! You always were the active one. So, are we still on for that family lunch next Saturday? We were talking about trying that new Italian place on Broad Street.

Okay, here's a conversation between the five friends in the Salford student flat, discussing their favourites, keeping in mind their dialects and backgrounds.   Setting:   A slightly cluttered student flat in Salford. Takeaway containers and textbooks are scattered around.   Characters:       Chloe :   South African-born, Northeast England dialect, Student.     Maisie :   Bishop Auckland, County Durham, Northeast England dialect, Student Nurse.     Saoirse :   From Ireland , Irish dialect, Student Nurse.     Bronwyn :   Penarth, Wales, Welsh dialect, Nursing.     Liv :   Hartlepool, County Durham, Northeast England dialect, Student Nurse.        Maisie:   Right, we're doing favourites, aren’t we? So, let's start easy. Favourite biscuit, go! I'm gonna have to go with a good old Jaffa Cake, proper dunk-able.   Liv:   Aye, Jaffa Cakes are champion. But for me, it’s gotta be a digestive. Plain, no fancy stuff, just a good, solid digestive. You can dunk it properly without it disintegrating.   Chloe:   You’re both so… sensible! I'm a McVitie's chocolate finger person all the way. That chocolate's the best. I used to get them for my gran back home. She loved ‘em, you know.   Saoirse:   Well, I'm gonna have to stir things up a bit. Tayto Crisps are my absolute favourite. The cheese and onion ones, mind. Nothing else will do. They're like… comfort food. Makes me miss home, though.   Bronwyn:   Right, well, that's a bit much for me! Tayto? I need something a bit more sophisticated, I think. I’d have to say Welsh cakes, definitely. My Nain used to make them fresh all the time. Warm, with sugar and butter…  shivers slightly  ...those were the days.   Maisie:   Welsh cakes, eh? Never tried 'em. Are they like… little pancakes?   Bronwyn:   Aye, a bit like that, but with dried fruits and spices. Very traditional! You’d love them, I reckon. We should try and bake some sometime.   Liv:   Speaking of baking, Chloe, your mum’s biltong recipe's still the best, isn't it? I keep trying to make it, but it's not the same.   Chloe:   Oh, stop it! It’s just a bit of air-dried meat, Liv. But yeah, Mum’s is special. I miss it loads. Sometimes the supermarkets here don't even have it.   Saoirse:   Air-dried meat? Sounds a bit… intense for my tastes! Do you guys have a favourite animal then? To lighten the mood?   Maisie:   Ooh, good one! Definitely a golden retriever.

Honestly, look at this. Another one of those ‘things you’ll regret not doing in your twenties’ lists. Skydiving, learning Mandarin, owning a vintage Vespa… like, who has the time? And the money? Don’t even start. I saw one that said, “Become a world-renowned artist!” As if that's just a hobby you pick up on a Tuesday. Exactly! And it’s all layered with this guilt. Like, if you’re not constantly expanding your horizons and achieving peak experience, you’re failing at being a young person. Tell me about it. I’m just trying to finish this essay on Sylvia Plath without having a complete existential crisis. World-renowned artist can wait. Speaking of which, how’s that essay going? Still wrestling with the bell jar metaphor? Kind of. I think I've got a decent angle on it now, just the writing feels…clunky. You know? Like I’m trying to force something that isn’t there. I know that feeling. Remember my history essay last term? I spent three days staring at a blank screen trying to explain the significance of the Treaty of Versailles. Oh god, yes! You looked like you were about to spontaneously combust. You should've just written about how frustrating it was to write about it. That’s probably more relatable. Maybe I should. At least it would be honest. You know, it's weird to think we'll be...old one day. Right. Deep thoughts for a Tuesday afternoon. What sparked that? Just, I was looking at my nan's photos the other day. She’s…she’s really not well. And it just hit me, like, that's going to be us eventually. Right, so you’re telling me you had a Christmas dinner… underwater? Not  literally  underwater, Elara. It was in the Philippines, down on the beach, near the coral reefs. Whoever found it was supposed to have good luck all year. Always ending with someone needing a trip to the dentist, I recall. Cultural differences are fascinating.
